title: Tencent AI Chief Warns Models Near Biology-Harm Threshold
summary: Tencent's Yao Shunyu warns frontier AI approaching capability line where cyber and biology abilities can cause real-world damage. Hy4 weights coming soon.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on November 4, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- Tencent chief AI scientist Yao Shunyu warned frontier AI is closing in on cyber and biology capability thresholds for real harm.
- Yao urged Chinese open-weight labs to prioritize safety, noting biology risks may be harder to manage than cyber risks.
- Tencent will release Hy4 weights and a safety-testing report in the coming days following the model's November 4 launch.


Tencent's chief AI scientist used a Hong Kong science symposium over the weekend to issue a stark warning: frontier AI systems are approaching a capability threshold where cyber and biology abilities could enable real-world harm. Yao Shunyu, 29, told the gathering Saturday that managing biology risks may prove harder than containing cyber threats, and urged Chinese labs releasing open-weight models to prioritize safety infrastructure.


## The Capability Threshold Warning


Speaking at the Hong Kong event, Yao said the cyber abilities of today's models and the soon-to-arrive biology capabilities "will reach a threshold where it's actually possible to do harm." The statement reflects growing concern among frontier lab researchers that AI systems are closing in on a line where offensive capabilities outpace defensive controls. Yao, who joined Tencent in 2025 after working on OpenAI's Operator and Deep Research projects, argued that biology risks present unique challenges because biological agents can self-replicate and spread beyond digital containment.


## The Open-Weight Safety Debate


Yao acknowledged Anthropic's case for keeping advanced models proprietary but suggested a mixed approach may work better in practice. He pointed to a recent case where Hugging Face turned to a Chinese open model for cybersecurity work after American closed models declined the task on guardrail grounds. The example highlights a tension in AI safety policy: restrictive safety filters can push security researchers toward less-controlled alternatives. Yao called on Chinese companies releasing open weights to invest in rigorous pre-release testing and red-teaming.


## Tencent Hy4 Release and Safety Testing


Tencent officially launched its flagship Hy4 model on November 4, 2026. The company says it excluded offensive hacking material from training data while retaining defensive security content. Internal reviewers reported strong basic biology knowledge but weaker performance at designing experiments, a finding that may limit near-term risks. Tencent plans to release Hy4 weights and a detailed safety-testing report in the coming days, a move that will allow external researchers to audit the model's capabilities and identify potential misuse vectors.


## Yao's Background and Influence


At 29, Yao is one of the youngest chief scientists leading frontier AI work at a major lab. His year at OpenAI gave him direct exposure to the safety debates shaping American AI policy, including Anthropic's decision to keep Claude models closed and OpenAI's tiered release strategy for GPT-4 and later systems. His call for Chinese labs to adopt similar caution carries weight given his insider perspective on both Western and Chinese AI development cultures.


**What this means:** Yao's warning signals that Tencent and other Chinese labs are tracking the same capability curves that have prompted safety concerns at Anthropic, OpenAI, and DeepMind. The decision to release Hy4 weights alongside a safety report suggests Tencent is testing a middle path between full openness and proprietary control. If biology capabilities do reach the threshold Yao described, expect intensified debate over whether open-weight releases remain viable for frontier models, or whether a new regulatory framework will be needed to gate access to the most capable systems.
